# F8: materials, textures and the data formats {#sec-fg-materials-formats}

The engine builds every visible surface from data files. A mod replaces a
texture or a material at load time, or swaps one at run time on a named
selection. This page states the replacement that works, the swap that fails,
the engine limits, and the visible defect a wrong value shows.

## What works

A PBO that carries a replacement `.paa` or `.rvmat` at a vanilla path
overrides the baked asset. Two PBOs that carry one path resolve to the
later-loaded file. This is the PBO path override {src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}.

The engine resolves a file path from its PBO prefix. AEE builds under
`z\aee\addons\`, so it does not collide with the vanilla `a3\` tree by
default. A deliberate override needs a PBO that mounts at the vanilla path
{src:adr:ADR-001}.

A class names its textureable parts in `hiddenSelections[]`. The matching
`hiddenSelectionsMaterials[]` adds one material per selection, with no model
edit {src:cfg:CfgVehicles>>hiddenSelectionsMaterials}. AEE reads the array and
maps each selection to its own material {src:script:addons/material/functions/fnc_getObjectMaterial.sqf}.

Two commands swap a surface at run time. `setObjectTexture` sets a texture on
one selection by index {src:cmd:setObjectTexture}. `setObjectMaterial` sets a
material the same way {src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}.

An RVMAT is a text material. It names a pixel shader, a vertex shader and one
texture per stage. The shared default material declares
`PixelShaderID = "Normal"`, `VertexShaderID = "Basic"` and a StageTI texture
{src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}.

A PAA is a compressed texture with a mip chain. `armake paa2img` converts a
PAA to an image, and `armake img2paa` converts an image to a PAA
{src:cmd:paa2img}. The tool writes DXT1, DXT3, DXT5, ARGB4444, ARGB1555 or
AI88.

## What does not work

A run-time material swap needs a selection. An object whose P3D names no
selection cannot take one. AEE cannot verify a model it does not hold, so this
config path stays unused {src:adr:ADR-001}.

Texture size has a hard limit. Each axis must be a power of two, and the
maximum is 4096 by 4096 {src:cmd:setObjectTexture}.

A material override cannot reach the baked terrain. `CfgSurfaces` defines
surface behaviour and carries no material field {src:cfg:CfgSurfaces>>Default}.

## Limitations

The terrain surface-type mask is baked into the WRP, not into config. No
config field and no script command reaches it, so a change needs a
re-binarised map {src:cfg:CfgSurfaces>>Default}.

The terrain's rendered material is the WRP layer RVMAT. Each terrain cell
carries one, and they ship in `map_altis_data_layers`
{src:pbo:Addons/map_altis_data_layers.pbo}.

The default TI material is one file. Every object with no dedicated thermal
map falls back to the shared `a3\data_f\default_vehicle_ti_ca.paa`
{src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}.

A material defines appearance and surface response, not physics. A surface
carries friction and no mass key {src:adr:ADR-037}.

## Breaks visually

A material on the wrong selection corrupts the picture. A per-selection swap
on the wrong index alters the visible appearance. This is the Zulu uniform
defect, issue #123 {src:adr:ADR-001}.

A bad PAA shows as a soft or speckled surface. A texture whose axes are not
powers of two, or a mip chain that loses detail, blurs the part at range
{src:cmd:paa2img}.

A length mismatch shifts every material. The engine reads
`hiddenSelectionsMaterials[]` per selection, so a short or long array paints
the wrong part {src:cfg:CfgVehicles>>hiddenSelectionsMaterials}.
